steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Context: "Macbeth" was written in 1606, early in James I's reign. The play reflects James's interests: witchcraft, kingship, and the dangers of treason. | Theatre was for everyone: Shakespeare wrote for all classes - high drama for nobility, jokes and action for groundlings. Plays needed to engage diverse audiences. | Relevance: "Macbeth" explores treason, regicide, and the betrayal of a king by a trusted subject. The Gunpowder Plot was fresh in the audience's minds. | Golden Rule: Link context to specific moments in the play. Don't just dump historical facts - explain how context deepens understanding of the text.
